title: Library System
statement:
Build a small library out of three classes that work together: a `Book` with an id and a title, a `Member` who borrows books, and a `Library` that lends books to members and takes them back. A member can hold at most 3 books at a time. The library supports four operations:

- `addBook id title` puts a new book on the shelf.
- `lend id name` lends the book `id` to the member `name`. It returns `lent` when that works. It returns `unavailable` when someone already has the book, even when it's the same member, and `limit reached` when the member already holds 3 books. Check whether the book is out first.
- `giveBack id` takes the book back and returns `returned`, or returns `not lent` when nobody has it.
- `booksOf name` returns the titles of the books the member holds, in the order they were lent and separated by spaces, or `none` when the member holds no books.

A member joins the first time the library sees their name, so `lend` and `booksOf` work for any name. Book ids are unique, titles and names are single words, and every id in a `lend` or `giveBack` was added before. Two books can share a title.

The first line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Print the answer to each `lend`, `giveBack`, and `booksOf` on its own line.

Input:

```text
9
addBook b1 Dune
addBook b2 Emma
lend b1 ana
lend b2 ana
lend b1 ben
booksOf ana
giveBack b1
lend b1 ben
booksOf ana
```

Expected output:

```text
lent
lent
unavailable
Dune Emma
returned
lent
Emma
```

hints: Give each class one job. A book knows who has it, a member knows which books they hold, and the library keeps every book by id and every member by name.
For `lend`, check the book first and the member's limit second, and only change anything when both checks pass. Then update both sides: the book's borrower and the member's list.
For `giveBack`, the book tells you who has it, so you can find that member and take the book off their list.
